title: The simulator QA overflow check flags hidden UI Toolkit elements
claim: The simulator's QA Test checks for horizontal overflow at 600x600. Meta's UI Toolkit keeps SubNavigationPager neighbour pages mounted beside the visible one, hidden and inert inside a clipping pager, and pads StaticContainer material canvases by 32 px, so with the documented 24 px content inset a full-width canvas spans -8 to 608 px.
actual: The check fails any element under body whose right edge is past 601 px, including hidden, inert, transparent and ancestor-clipped elements. On a stock Toolkit app every pager tab except the last fails with "div overflows right edge", and a screen with a StaticContainer fails with "canvas overflows right edge", although nothing can scroll sideways. The Toolkit validator reports no findings and forbids restyling Toolkit internals, so the app cannot fix it.
impact: Apps that use the Toolkit as documented fail the simulator's quality checklist.
workaround: Treat these two findings as false positives after checking by hand that nothing scrolls sideways.
repro: Initializer app with a SubNavigationPager of 3 items at the root route: run the QA Test on any tab but the last. Then a ScrollView with padding-inline var(--uit-spacing-large) holding one full-width StaticContainer.
